flags.reason: The guide’s States description says “Give the group data, renderItem, keyExtractor, and onDragEnd, and every row gets a drag handle.”, but the installed ListGroup.tsx (0.1.78-dbe0e02, ReorderRow, lines 163–210) wraps each row in a plain Animated.View and adds no handle: the handle is the List Item’s, shown when renderItem returns it with isDraggable and onDragHandleGrant={drag}, as the guide’s own example and the evidence do. The entry leaves the sentence out and cites the evidence for the handle. Guide fix #526. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch8, for Marcin to confirm.

examples.purpose: Payments, a month at a time, the guide’s In context: a history screen stacks one group per month, newest first; each label names the month, and each row opens that payment (onPress). Each row’s amount is a MoneyValue in trailing; the rows carry no modes, so they take the group’s.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <ListGroup label="March 2025">
    <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Netflix" supportText="12 Mar" trailing={<MoneyValue value="499" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
    <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Swiggy" supportText="10 Mar" trailing={<MoneyValue value="320" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
    <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Adani Electricity" supportText="8 Mar" trailing={<MoneyValue value="1,840" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
  </ListGroup>
  <ListGroup label="February 2025">
    <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Jio Fiber" supportText="28 Feb" trailing={<MoneyValue value="999" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
    <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Zomato" supportText="14 Feb" trailing={<MoneyValue value="650" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
  </ListGroup>
</VStack>

from.quote: A history screen stacks one group per month, newest first. Each label names the month, and each row opens that payment.

examples.purpose: Rows people can reorder, the guide’s States: data, renderItem, keyExtractor and onDragEnd are all given; each row is a ListItem with a drag handle (isDraggable, onDragHandleGrant from drag, isDragging while it is the dragged row). onDragEnd (a stub here) hands your screen the new order to save, and data is that order. The group passes no modes in this mode, and no row sets any, so every row has the same.
examples.jsx:
<ListGroup
  label="Pinned on home"
  data={[
    { id: 'Savings', title: 'Savings', support: 'Balance and statements', icon: 'ic_savings' },
    { id: 'Bills', title: 'Bills', support: 'Electricity, water, gas', icon: 'ic_bill' },
    { id: 'Mobile recharge', title: 'Mobile recharge', support: 'Jio prepaid', icon: 'ic_mobile' },
    { id: 'Wallet', title: 'Wallet', support: 'JioPay wallet', icon: 'ic_wallet' },
  ]}
  keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
  onDragEnd={() => {}}
  renderItem={({ item, isActive, drag }) => (
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      title={item.title}
      supportText={item.support}
      navArrow={false}
      isDraggable
      isDragging={isActive}
      onDragHandleGrant={drag}
      leading={<IconCapsule iconName={item.icon} />}
    />
  )}
/>

from.quote: People drag a row by its handle, and onDragEnd hands your screen the new order to save.

props.name: label
props.description: None by default. Shown above the rows on one line with an ellipsis; disableTruncation lets it wrap. 12 px (listGroup/gap) below it when there are rows.

props.name: modes
props.description: The group passes them to every row ({ ...group, ...row }, so a row’s own modes win), and List Items pass them on to their slots. Not in reorder mode: rows aren’t given the group’s modes there.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Dropped: the root is a list with no name, and the label text is hidden from screen readers (#420).

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

props.name: data
props.description: Reorder mode: the rows’ items, with keyExtractor, renderItem and onDragEnd. All four, or the group silently renders only the label. Rows aren’t given the group’s modes in this mode.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Reorder mode: returns each row. Each row shows a drag handle (List Item isDraggable, onDragHandleGrant={drag}).

props.name: onDragEnd
props.description: Reorder mode: gets the new order on release; the screen saves it.

props.name: ...ListGroupStaticProps | ListGroupReorderProps<T>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection ListGroup reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: List Item Style
modes.description: Default: rows 42 px tall, no fill, 12 px gap. Boxed: rows get 12 px padding, a white fill, a 1 px #ebebed border and radius 12 (68 px tall), gap 12. Minimal: gap 4 and regular-weight titles. The look comes from List Item; the group only changes its gap. Declared: A token collection ListGroup reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Title Level
modes.description: Default: the label is 14/18 medium #24262b. Bold: 18/22 black #0d0d0f. Declared: A token collection ListGroup reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: children
slots.description: The rows, stacked full width, 12 px apart. children or listGroupSlot (listGroupSlot’s rows first when both). Only elements survive: strings vanish.

gaps.text: Figma shows a “March 2025” title; the package (and Storybook’s Default) has no label until you pass one.
Code Connect maps Figma’s List Group, but not its Title to label.
The listGroup/border/color token exists, but the code hard-codes a transparent border.
Static mode passes the group’s modes to its rows; reorder mode doesn’t (Component Bug #420).
Reorder mode needs all four of data, keyExtractor, renderItem and onDragEnd; leave one out and the group silently renders only the label (Component Bug #420).
